turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The processing route dominates.** The 300 samples fall into distinct heat-treatment regimes with very different fatigue levels:

- As-rolled/normalized only (THT=30, no Q&T): 225–275 MPa
- Quench & temper (THT≈845–865, TT=550–680): 325–643 MPa
- High-Si spring-steel Q&T (C≈0.53–0.63, Si≈1.3–2.05, TT=420–500): 688–906 MPa
- **Carburized/case-hardened (NT=CT=930, THT=30, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5): 838–1190 MPa** ← clearly the winning route

So I fix the carburizing "envelope" shared by all top rows: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Tt=120, TCr=0.5.

**2. Process effects within the carburized block** (matched-composition comparisons):

- **TT=160 > TT=200** every time: +47, +20, +40, +36 MPa across four compositions. No data exists below 160, so I stay at 160 rather than gamble on an untempered part.
- For the best composition, **Ct=540 + QmT=140 beats Ct=469.8 + QmT=60: 1190 vs 1124** — both sit at the favorable range boundary (deepest case, hottest quench medium).
- DT=850 / Dt=15 (the lowest reheat temperature and shortest hold in the block — fine prior-austenite grain, less retained austenite) is what the two top rows use.

**3. Composition effects.** Averaging each steel over its process variants, the ranking is roughly: L (1157) > K (1100) ≈ J (1094) > G (1043) ≈ I (1048) > H (1018) > … > A/C (~876–880). The two best steels share: C≈0.21–0.23, Si≈0.31–0.35, Mo≈0.17–0.18, low P, RedRatio 690–860, dA 0.06–0.08, dB≤0.01, dC=0. The overall best ("L") is the high-Ni variant: **Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Mn=0.51, Si=0.35, RedRatio=860 (block max), dA=0.07**. Notably, very high Ni (2.6–2.78) in the Q&T block does *not* help, and the high-Cr variant (K) tops out lower (1144), so I keep L's exact chemistry rather than push Ni/Cr further.

**4. Where I deliberately don't extrapolate.** RedRatio=860, Si=0.35, Ni=1.69, C=0.23 are already the block maxima associated with the best results; the global ranges (RedRatio 5530, Si 2.05, C 0.63) only occur in inferior routes, so extending them is unsupported. The one small, physically justified tweak: **dB=0.0 instead of 0.01** — B-type (alumina) inclusions are the most fatigue-detrimental, and the second-best steel (K, 1144 MPa) already runs dB=0 with the same dA/dC profile.

This recipe reproduces the observed global maximum (1190 MPa) with a marginal cleanliness improvement.

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.0, dC=0.0
